title: I'm building a realistic bodycam FPS in Godot with Claude Opus 5.5. This is how far I've gotten.
author: Sweet-Chip6849
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I wanted to share something I've been working really hard on lately.

It's called **Flow Fire Bodycam**, a first-person shooter inspired by real police bodycam footage.

My goal is to recreate that feeling of being right there when everything suddenly goes wrong. The camera movement, the gunshots, the lighting, the way people react... I want all of it to feel as believable as possible.

I'm building it in Godot with AI coding agents, mainly Claude Opus 5.5. I direct the development, decide what needs to change, test the game myself, and keep refining things until they actually feel right.

One of the coolest things we've built is a custom testing system that lets the AI run the game, record footage, measure things like recoil and camera movement, and compare results without me having to manually test every little change.

I've spent the last few days focusing almost entirely on realism, and the difference compared to the previous version is honestly crazy to me haha.

I'm also trying to optimize it as much as possible. One of my biggest goals is to achieve this kind of visual experience on PCs without expensive dedicated GPUs.

It's still a very early pre-alpha, and there's a lot left to improve.

Here's some actual gameplay!

I'd love to know what you guys think. Does the camera and gunplay look convincing? What would you improve first?

And if you're also making games with AI agents, I'd love to hear how you handle testing.

**Game page:** [https://masterinc.itch.io/flow-fire-bodycam-pre-alpha](https://masterinc.itch.io/flow-fire-bodycam-pre-alpha)
